title: Exact sections identify principal derived reduction with the actual scalar-extension unit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with final object $U$, and suppose $\Gamma=\Gamma(U,-)$ is exact on abelian sheaves. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t\in R$ such that multiplication by $t$ on $R$ is injective. Put $A=R/(t)$ with its specified quotient map. Let $\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ be a surjection of sheaves of commutative rings and let $R\to\Gamma(\mathcal O)$, $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal O')$ be compatible coefficient maps. Assume $0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{t}\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'\to0$ is exact, with $\mathcal O'=\mathcal O/t\mathcal O$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and exact coefficient restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $G:D(\mathcal O)\to D(R)$ and $G':D(\mathcal O')\to D(A)$ be exact sections with these scalar restrictions. Write $T=-\otimes^L_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ and $L=-\otimes_R^LA$ with the normalized extension/restriction adjunctions [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. For every $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ there is a natural isomorphism $\alpha_N:LGN\xrightarrow{\sim}G'TN$ satisfying
$$\operatorname{Res}_{R\to A}(\alpha_N)\circ u_{GN}=G(v_N),$$
where $u$ and $v$ are the ordinary-module and sheaf derived scalar-extension units and exact sections identify the two restricted targets. This specifies $\alpha_N$ uniquely as the scalar-extension adjunct of $G(v_N)$. Its normalization on any flat-term K-flat sheaf resolution $P\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] is $\theta_P\circ c_{\Gamma P}$ as defined in [lem-pod-derived-reduction-sheaf-resolution-independence]: $\theta_P$ sends a section modulo $t$ to its quotient section. On any flat-term K-flat ordinary-module resolution $q:Q\to\Gamma P$, the resulting representative is $Q/tQ\to\Gamma(P/tP)$, $\bar x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$, and its adjunct is $Q\to\Gamma(P/tP)$, $x\mapsto q(x)\bmod t$. These formulas are independent of both resolutions; no K-flatness of $\Gamma P$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose the normalized ordinary sheaf coefficient adjunction. Apply the resolving-class derived-adjunction theorem to sheaf K-flat complexes, using K-flat resolutions and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms by coefficient extension. Transport the resulting derived adjunction to the specified functor T and counit epsilon: the universal comparison is invertible on K-flat models, and hence on all derived objects by resolutions and naturality. This preserves the normalized transpose formula for every cochain map. Do the same for L and its mixed-tensor counit, using ordinary K-flat resolutions, extension of scalars on K-flat quasi-isomorphisms, and the K-flat computation of the mixed-tensor counit. Evaluating the transpose formulas on identities gives both required unit formulas.

proof.text: Define beta as the adjoint mate of the derived restriction square. The mate identity gives exactly the required unit equation and the adjunction bijection gives uniqueness. On ordinary sheaves define the tensor-to-quotient-sections map by a tensor x going to a times the quotient section of x. Its transpose is sections of the ordinary sheaf unit, checked on 1 tensor x. Apply the normalized derived-mate comparison theorem: on any flat-term K-flat P the map beta equals the existing alpha_P, since the ordinary comparison equals theta_P on pure tensors. Thus beta is already natural for all derived morphisms without a common-refinement argument.

proof.text: For a flat sheaf M, tensor the coefficient short exact sequence with M and apply exact sections. Its first map is multiplication by t on sections, so t is injective on Gamma(M). For any ordinary complex K with termwise injective t, resolve K by a flat-term K-flat Q. Regularity of t on R implies regularity on each flat module Q^i (Mathlib Module.Flat.isSMulRegular_of_isRegular, valid for any commutative ring). The principal-quotient quasi-isomorphism lemma makes extension of Q to A quasi-isomorphic to extension of K. Naturality of the mixed-tensor counit, its invertibility on Q, and the invertibility of L(q) imply that c_K is invertible. Consequently alpha_P is invertible for every flat-term K-flat P. Resolve an arbitrary derived object by such a P; naturality of beta shows its component there is invertible as well, giving the required natural isomorphism.

proof.text: For any ordinary cochain map q into Gamma(P), extension followed by theta sends 1 tensor x to the quotient section of q(x), and its ordinary adjunct sends x to the same section. Substitute beta_P = alpha_P, cancel the derived-model and sections-factor isomorphisms, and apply counit naturality to obtain the required derived representative equation. The normalized derived transpose formula of step 2 yields its adjunct equation. Finally beta naturality along any sheaf-resolution quasi-isomorphism p, together with beta_P = alpha_P, identifies the existing resolvedComparison with beta_M. This proves independence of both resolutions, without assuming that Gamma(P) is K-flat.
